pairs.subject: native-guest-interop
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs:193 The host reaches its only guest code (the WebView2 frontend) through Tauri's serialized IPC command handler; nothing embeds a guest language runtime with a collected heap. I searched apps/desktop/src-tauri and crates/table-os for boa_engine, rquickjs, NativeFunction, from_copy_closure, JsValue, v8:: and gc::Trace and found no hits, and neither Cargo.toml lists a guest-engine dependency. So the subject's precondition (a host value or closure living inside guest-heap cells) does not hold here.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs:193 Host values never go into collected guest cells; they cross as serde-serialized IPC payloads.
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs:193 No host closure is registered on a guest heap; guest-callable functions are #[tauri::command] fns dispatched by name.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native/commands.rs:5 Per-context host state comes from Tauri's typed managed State, not from downcasting a type-erased guest-object payload. No guest objects carry host payloads.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native/commands.rs:3 Async commands do become JS promises, but only through IPC serialization in a separate webview process. No promise job settles inside an embedded heap, so this belongs to the ipc-contract subject.
